answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake that decays if the agent misbehaves - like a farmer tending an orchard, the stake only grows with honest work. An identity that appears overnight and floods the ocean of requests with spam has no history to vouch for it, while one that survived the long cold tundra of repeated audits earns reputation that cheap clones cannot fake. Costly, time-tested identity beats free copies.
